text: […] [May] El Elyon bless you and your sons.
Your descendants will endure; all the righteous and upright […].
[…] injustice and every deceit will no longer be found […].
Now take the tablets and read everything written on them. I took the tablets, read them, and […] all my troubles […].
[…] everything that will come upon me during the one hundred and forty-seven years of my life. Then he told me: ‘Take a tablet from my hand.’
I took this tablet from his hand, read it all, and saw written in it: ‘This place will not be built as a sanctuary […].’
[…] When you bring the offerings on the appointed day, they will not be empty before El Elyon […].
[…] [The surviving words here cannot be translated.]
[…] in the land; you will eat its fruit and all its goodness, and live […].
[…] to turn aside, to stray, and to walk in paths of error […].
[…] in your wickedness, until you stand before him […].
[…] [The surviving letters do not permit a reliable translation.]
[…] how the building will be […], and how their priests will be clothed and made pure […].
[…] their hands [will be purified]; they will offer sacrifices on the altar, and throughout the land they will eat a portion of their sacrifices […].
[…] how they will draw water that comes out from the city and from beneath its walls, and where they will pour it […].
[…] before me: a land divided into two portions […].
[…] [The remaining letters are not readable enough to translate.]
